title: Which values went missing?
hook: Hide the same number of salaries under two different selection rules.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: random gaps vs gaps caused by the value itself give opposite biases.

misconception: Treating why is data missing? as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: random gaps vs gaps caused by the value itself give opposite biases.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Five salaries are 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. If the two largest are missing, what mean is calculated from the visible salaries?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-why-is-data-missing/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Full salaries [20,30,40,50,60], mean 40. Remove 20 and 60 (mean 40), or remove 50 and 60 (mean 30). Show every missing slot and why missingness matters.

src/demos/probability/p100-why-is-data-missing/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Full salaries [20,30,40,50,60], mean 40. Remove 20 and 60 (mean 40), or remove 50 and 60 (mean 30). Show every missing slot and why missingness matters.

claims.text: The retained means are 30 when large values are hidden and 40 when the two extremes are hidden. The full five-value mean is 40.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-why-is-data-missing/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Full salaries [20,30,40,50,60], mean 40. Remove 20 and 60 (mean 40), or remove 50 and 60 (mean 30). Show every missing slot and why missingness matters.

claims.text: What disappears matters as much as how much disappears. This finite illustration compares two explicit selection rules; the balanced second rule is not a promise that random missingness is exactly unbiased in every sample.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-why-is-data-missing/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Full salaries [20,30,40,50,60], mean 40. Remove 20 and 60 (mean 40), or remove 50 and 60 (mean 30). Show every missing slot and why missingness matters.

claims.text: Data are 2, 4, 6, 8. Hide only 8. What mean remains? The visible mean is (2+4+6)/3=4, below the full mean 5.
